rows.author: C039
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR AN INCREASED SPECIAL GROUP TERM INSURANCE COVERAGE FOR THE MEMBERS OF THE ARMED FORCES OF THE PHILIPPINES INCLUDING THE MEMBERS OF THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL POLICE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 352, AS AMENDED,AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Through a Presidential Decree (PD352) issued by former President Ferdinand Marcos, a Special Group Term Insurance was created for the members of the Armed Forces of the Philippines which was designed to help its members, in the form of wake and burial assistance in the amount of Six Thousand Pesos (P6,000.00). In 1905, by another executive fiat (PD 1965), the amount was raised to Twelve Thousand Pesos (P12,000.00). Admittedly, a militiaman is covered by the compulsory insurance granted by the Government Service Insurance Sytem, the same however, is NOT enough for the sustenance of a grieving widow and her children.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C039
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING RETIREMENT BENENFITS TO ELECTED AND APPOINTED LOCAL GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS INCLUDING BARANGAY TANODS WHO HAVE RENDERED THREE FULL TERMS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991 AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREOF
rows.abstract: ALL ELECTED AND APPOINTED LOCAL GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS INCLUDING BARANGAY TANODS, SHALL BE ENTITLED TO GSIS RETIREMENT BENEFITS PROVIDED, THAT THEY HAVE RENDERED NO LESS THAN THREE FULL TERMS AS ELECTED OR APPOINTED BARANGAY OFFICIAL.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C039
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE REGULARIZATION OF EMPLOYEES, PROHIBITING CONTRACTUAL OR LABOR-ONLY CONTRACTING FOR REGULAR POSITIONS, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSER ARTICLES 280 AND 281 OF THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to amend Articles 280 and 281 of the Labor Code to make sure that all workers would come to enjoy the benefits of regularization when due. This would give workers the necessary boost in their daily toil. This would prevent unscrupulous employers from getting around the law just to deny workers the benefits of regularization. This bill seeks to correct the lopsided disarity of economic interest between the employer and employee to promote social justice in the labor front.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09168) enacted on 2002-06-07
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROVIDE PROTECTION TO NEW PLANT VARIETIES, ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL PLANT VARIETY PROTECTION BOARD AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The State recongizes that an effective intellectual property system in general and the development of new plant variety in particular is vital in attaining food security for the country. To this end, it shall protect and secure the exclusive rights of breeders with respect to their new plant variety particularly when beneficial to the people for such periods as provided for in this Act.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04518

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROTECT AND PROMOTE THE HEALTH OF THE PEOPLE THROUGH THE PREVENTION, CONTROL AND ABATEMENT OF AIR POLLUTION CAUSED BY SMOKE-BELCHING VEHICLES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1181, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: In line with this constitutional mandate, this bill proposes the imposition of an additional requirement before a vehicle's registration will be allowed or renewed. The requirement of subjecting the vehicle to a smoke belching test for its initial registration and every year thereafter will minimize, if not totally eradicate, air pollution caused by smoke-belching vehicles.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECOLOGY since 2001-07-24

rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECOLOGY since 2001-07-24

rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2003-05-21, transmitted to on 2003-05-22 and received by the Senate on 2003-05-27
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE PLANTING OF TREES IN OPEN SPACES OF SUBDIVISION PROJECTS DEVELOPED FOR RESIDENTIAL, INDUSTRIAL OR COMMERCIAL PURPOSE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Greening Act of  2001." Every owner of land subdivided and devleoped for residential, industrial, or comercial purpose shall reserve develop, and maintain at least thirty percent (30%) of the gross area as open space for parks, playgrounds , recreational uses, schools, roads, places of worship, hospitals, health centers, barangay centers, and other similar amenities.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05812

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING LOCAL GOVERNMENTS TO PLANT TREES ALONG NATIONAL AND LOCAL HIGHWAYS WITHIN ITS TERRITORIAL BOUNDARIES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "The Greening of Philippine Highways Act of 2001." It shall be the primary responsibility of local government, with the cooperation of the Department of Interior and Local Government, Department of Environment and Natural Resources, Department of Public Works and Highways and other concerned government agencies, to plant and maintain indigenous Philippine trees along national and local highways within their respective territorial boundaries.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECOLOGY since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071

rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING INCENTIVES TO SUBDIVISION HOMEOWNERS ASSOCIATIONS TO DEVELOP AND MAINTAIN FORESTED AREAS WITHIN THEIR SUBDIVISIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: This bill seeks to expand  the area to be devoted to the preservation of the ecological balance of nature. In reserving a whole area for such activity, and by getting the community members involved, it is hoped that there would eventuallybe a sincere appreciation for a healthy, clean and natural environment.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05844

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO CONSERVE AND PROTECT THE PUBLIC FORESTS, MANGROVES AND WILDLIFE THEREIN THROUGH A PROGRAM OF RENEWAL, REFORESTATION AND REPLANTING AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill provides for classification and percentages allocation of public forests. The object of this bill is to rehabilitate public forest lands and revert areas presently denuded and eroded to become thriving forest reserves.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF PARKS AND MINI-PARKS IN BARANGAYS, MUNICIPALITIES, CITIES AND PROVINCES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to create a NATIONAL PARKS AND MINI-PARKS DEVELOPMENT COMMITTEE which shall tap any or all government agencies, corporations and instrumentaliti es, non-governmenta l organizations (NGOs), peoples organizations (POs), the Governor'sLeague of the Philippines, Mayor's League of the Philippines and the Barangay Association of the Philippines as local communities to provide resources and assistance in the implementation of this Act.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE REGULATION AND DISPOSAL OF MEDICAL WASTES, DECLARING CERTAIN ACTS UNLAWFUL, PRESCRIBING PENALTIES THERETO, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to regulate medical wastes by empowering the Secretary of Health to establish acceptable standards for its management and disposal. It likewise strengthens the ability of the Department of Health in dealing with the issue of medicalwaste management, and impose stiff penalties for the mindless disposal of dangerous medical waste.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECOLOGY since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING AS UNLAWFUL THE USE OF POLYCARBON PLASTICS, STYROFOAM AND OTHER SYNTHETIC MATERIALS HARMFUL TO THE ENVIRONMENT AND ESTABLISHING A CRITERION FOR THE ENDORSEMENT OF ENVIRONMENT FRIENDLY CONSUMER PRODUCTS
rows.abstract: Rationale: Styrofoam, the most common synthetic material in popular use by fastfood chains and product packagers, is not as benign as we have long thought it to be. Left undisposed, it continually releases chlorofluorocar bons, more commonly refersto as CFCs into the atmosphere. Choloflourocarb ons are the same elements found in aerosol propellants and freon refrigerants, that have been conclusively linked to the thinning of the ozone layer in the earth's atmosphere.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECOLOGY since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09175) enacted on 2002-11-07
rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE OWNERSHIP, POSSESSION, SALE, IMPORTATION AND USE OF CHAIN SAWS, PENALIZING VIOLATIONS THEREOF AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: It takes more than fifty (50) years to grow a Phiilippine mahogany tree into harvestable size but it takes less than five (5) minutes to fell and buck the same tree into logs with the use of a chainsaw. A chainsaw, therefore, becomes a handy tool for illegal loggers and even professional kaingineros to advance their trade. Skilled operators of chainsaws use the machine not only for cutting down trees but also for sawing the logs into tablon or rough lumber.
rows.status: Substituted by HB03994

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE MANUFACTURE, DISTRIBUTION, SALE OR USE OF AEROSOL CONTAINING CHLOROFLOUROCAR BONS AND PROVIDING PENALTY FOR THE VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: The manufacture, distribution, sale or use in the country of aerosol containing chloroflourocar bons (CFC's) is hereby prohibited to reduce global emission of a substance that causes damage to the stratospheric ozone layer.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2003-05-21, transmitted to on 2003-05-22 and received by the Senate on 2003-05-27
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE COASTAL ENVIRONMENT PROGRAM, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Coastal environments encompass different ecosystems such as shore lands, mangroves, seagrass beds and coral reefs. They are among the most productive and biologiocally diverse landscapes known to man. In an archipelagic country like the Philippines, where over 80% of the major settlements are located within ten or twenty kilometers from the shorelines, coastal environments are critical and often dominant ecological presuppositions of economic, social and cultural life. Thus, the protection and proper management of coastal environments are important concerns of the State and are explicitly mandated by the Constitution.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05493

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A NATIONAL ECOTOURISM POLICY, ESTABLISHING A FRAMEWORK FOR ITS INSTITUTIONALIZ ATION, CREATING MECHANISM FOR ITS IMPLEMENTATION AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The richness of our resources could only be optimally utilized if they are best protected. Tourism would yield the most profits if it ensures the primary of the environment and the preservation of the culture of our people. It is but timethat we reorient our tourism goals to a low-impact and sustainable type of tourism before nothing else would be left to us.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECOLOGY since 2001-07-24

first_reading.comm_act: jt. ref'l as per J.37; p.19

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING PUBLIC RECREATIONAL PARKS IN MAJOR URBAN AREAS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to establish at least one (1) public recreational park in every major urban center including, but not limited to, Metro Manila, Metro Cebu and Metro Davao. Such public recreational park shall comprise a picnic arrea and such other outdoor and indoor sports, health and recreational facilities as may be determined by the administering body hereafter designated in consultation with the appropriate government agencies, and workers' and employees groups.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC WORKS AND HIGHWAYS since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING A NATIONAL FRAMEWORK FOR THE PROTECTION OF BIODIVERSITY IN TERRESTRIAL, AQUATIC AND AGRICULTURAL RESOURCES AND CREATING THE INSTITUTIONAL MECHANISM FOR ITS IMPLEMENTATION
rows.abstract: Rationale: It is the policy of the State to conserve the biodiversity of the existing terrestial, aquatic and agricultural resources of the country, document the remaining flora and fauna therein, identify their medicinal and commercial uses and regulate their collection and utilization for the benefit of present and future generations of Filipino citizens.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE, FOOD & FISHERIES since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2002-04-23, transmitted to on 2002-04-29 and received by the Senate on 2002-04-30
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PRESERVATION, REFORESTATION, AFFORESTATION AND SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT OF MANGROVE FORESTS IN THE PHILIPPINES, PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This measure proposes to establish reservation areas in all coastal areas in each municipality of the country solely for the preservation, protection, reforestation, afforestation and sustainable development of mangrove forests. In setting aside portions of land for mangroves, we can ensure that our people will continue to enjoy the benefits accorded by this important ecosystem.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04359

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING FOREST MANAGEMENT, UTILIZATION, CONSERVATION AND PRESERVATION CENTERS IN PROVINCES INHABITED PREDOMINANTLY BY MEMBERS OF INDIGENOUS CULTURAL COMMUNITIES FAMILIES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Indigenous cultural communities in the country have proven their effectiveness in such efforts through the employment of indigenous customs and practices. Thus, the establishment of forest management centers in provinces predominantly populated by members of indigenous cultural communities. This aims to enhance forest rehabilitation, protection, and conservation by building on indigenous practices of doing the same.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE OFFICE OF ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION, DEFINING ITS FUNCTIONS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill will create a massive and comprehensive education and training campaign needed for the success of public policy on environmental issues. Through popularization of the issues, private initiative in the protection of the environment will beenhanced. Hence its immediate passage is most urgently requested.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PROTECTION AND CONSERVATION OF ALL OBJECTS OF UNDERWATER CULTURAL HERITAGE IN PHILIPPINE WATERS
rows.abstract: This bill aims to protect and preserve our underwater cultural heritage by providing for general requirements for underwater archaeology, exploration, and excavation. This measure also proposes the formulation of rules for the description of the items to be protected, prohibition of certain activities in the vicinity of a protected item or site, the establishment of a reward system for verified reports, and the imposition of sanction and penalties for the abuse of our underwater cultural heritage.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2002-05-07, transmitted to on 2002-05-09 and received by the Senate on 2002-05-13
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXPANDING THE PROHIBITED ACTS OF DISCRIMINATION AGAINST WOMEN ON ACCOUNT OF SEX, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE, ARTICLES 135 AND 137 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 442, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: The proposed bill, in keeping with the policy to eliminate sex-based discrimination in employment, penalizes an employer who favors a male employee oever a female employee, whether through notices, announcements or advertisements for employment or in the actual hiring or admission of workers, thus bringing about a step towards equitable employemnt opportunity for all.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04590

first_reading.comm_act: change of cttee. ref'l as per J.37; p.20

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE SERVICE OF WARRANTS OF ARREST IN CERTAIN CASES AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF
rows.abstract: Except only in cases of citizen's arrest, arrest of persons made as a result of surveillance and/or entrapment operations; persons being arrested for subversion and other crimes and offenses against national security; notorious and dangerous criminals for whom outstanding warrants of arrest have been issued; and escapists anf fugitives from justice, it is hereby prohibited to serve warrants of arrests during nighttime, on legal holidays or on weekends.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.mother_status: Bill reported out 2004-06-11 (#02161);Submitted by CIVIL, POLITICAL AND HUMAN RIGHTS
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A MANDATORY COURSE IN HUMAN RIGHTS FOR ALL OFFICERS, MEMBERS AND TRAINEES OF THE ARMED FORCES OF THE PHILIPPINES (AFP), THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL POLICE (PNP), THE NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION (NBI), AND OTHER LAW ENFORCEMENTAGENCIES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP), the Philippine National Police (PNP), the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP), the Bureau of Corrections (BuCor), and other law enforcement agencies shall include the study of human rights as an integral part of the education and training of all trainees/propse ctive members of such agencies. > No trainee and/or prospective member of the AFP, PNP, NBI. BJMP, BuCOR and other law enforcement agenciesshall be admitted into the service without passing a comprehensive examination on human rights to be administered by the Commission on Human Rights (CHR).
rows.status: Substituted by HB06721

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 12 (B) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8282, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE SOCIAL SECURITY ACT OF 2001
rows.abstract: This bill refers to the pension benefits of SSS members. The bill states that MEMBERS WITH MORE THAN TWENTY (20) CREDITED YEARS OF SERVICE SHALL HAVE AN INCREASE OF ONE THOUSAND TWO HUNDRED PESOS (P1,200.00) IN THEIR PENSION FOR EVERY ADDITIONAL TEN(10) CREDITED YEARS OF SERVICE.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2001-12-19, transmitted to on 2002-01-02 and received by the Senate on 2002-01-02
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO AMEND REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8239, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE PHILIPPINE PASSPORT ACT OF 1996
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to amend the provisions relating to the requirement for issuance of passports as well as additional ground for its amendment, suspension and revocation. Furthermore, the proposed bill enumerates the individuals who are qualified to file applications on behalf of certain applicants. The bill also seeks to penalize those who do damage to the Philippine passport's integrity and validity by punishing those who sell passport applications, government forms, as well as lost or stolen travel documents.
rows.status: Substituted by HB00434

rows.author: D071
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2003-12-17, transmitted to on 2003-12-18 and received by the Senate on 2004-01-06
rows.title_full: AN ACT RESTRUCTURING THE FISCAL INCENTIVES UNDER EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 226, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE OMNIBUS INVESTMENTS CODE OF 1987, AS AMENDED, AMENDING PERTINENT ARTICLES OF THE CODE, PROVIDING FOR PENALTIES IN VIOLATION THEREOF, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to EXTEND the period of tax holidays to a maximum of ten (10) years for pioneer firms, and eight (8) years for non-pioneer firms with the hope that potential investors may consider our country as the best venue for their commercial operations. "Tax holidays" refers to the EXEMPTION granted by the National Government from the imposition of corporate income tax on certain enterprises.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06011

first_reading.comm_act: jt. ref'ls as per J.17;p.15( Aug. 28,2001)

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROMOTE, DEVELOP AND ASSIST MICRO AND COTTAGE INDUSTRIES BY PROVIDING AN EFFECTIVE AND RATIONAL SYSTEM TO ADDRESS THEIR PRODUCTION AND TECHNOLOGY NEEDS
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to stimulate the establishment and sustain the growth of micro and cottage enterprises by addressing their production-rela ted needs. The systematic efficient and rational provision of assistance aimed at increasing productivity andavailability of these enterprises will in turn generate more employment, exports and to achieve countryside industrializait on.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES STOCK EXCHANGE
rows.abstract: This bill aims to assist small and medium entperises (SMES) in obtaining their financing requirements from the developing capital market in the country.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A COMPREHENSIVE CONSERVATION, PROTECTION, UTILIZATION, DEVELOPMENT AND MANAGEMENT OF THE PHILIPPINE EXCLUSIVE ECONOMIC ZONE (EEZ)
rows.abstract: This bill substantiates the State policy to protect our nation's martime wealth in its archipelagic waters, territorial sea and exclusive economic zone (EEZ). This bill also provides for our soverign rights and jurisdiction over the EEZ.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PROTECTION OF LAYOUT-DESIGNS (TOPOGRAPHIES) OF INTEGRATED CIRCUITS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE CERTAIN SECTIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8293, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Layout-Design" is synonymous with "topography" and means the three-dimension al disposition, however expressed, of the elements, at least one of which is an active element, and of some or all of the interconnection s of an integrated circuit, or such a three-dimension al disposition prepared for an integrated circuit intended for manufacture. Rationale: The reasons for assuring protection of lay-out designs of integrated circuits are: (1) to reward the creator; (2) to provide incentive for thecreation.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09178) enacted on 2002-11-13
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE MAGNA CARTA FOR COUNTRYSIDE AND BARANGAY BUSINESS ENTERPRISES (CBBEs), GRANTING EXEMPTIONS FROM ANY AND ALL GOVERNMENT RULES AND REGULATIONS AND PROVIDING INCENTIVES AND BENEFITS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Countryside and barangay business enteprises (CBBEs) are those engaged in the production, processing or manufacturing of products with a capitalization of not more than P50,000.00. > to encourage its formation and growth in the countryside, the government should grant non-tax incentives to CBBEs such as access to credit capitalization, technical training support and marketing assistance. This would generate more employment opportunities, help increase the income of the rural people,promote the market for indigenous products.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04871

rows.author: D071
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2003-12-17, transmitted to on 2003-12-18 and received by the Senate on 2004-01-06
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ENCOURAGE THE PARTICIPATION OF NON-GOVERNMENTA L ORGANIZATIONS (NGOs) AND STRENGTHEN THEIR ROLE IN NATIONAL DEVELOPMENT AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Assistance to NGOs may consist of: (1) Project Grants; (2) Matching Crants; (3) Concessional Loans; (4) technical, training and organizational development support; and (5) Such other assistance or support as may be determined to be appropriate and proper by the Secretary or Head of the Department, Commission or Agency.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06459

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A STUDENT FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE PROGRAM FOR STUDENTS OF ECONOMICALLY DISADVANTAGED FAMILIES AND AUTHORIZING THE APPROPRIATION OF FUNDS FOR THE PURPOSE
rows.abstract: The term "economically disadvantaged but deserving students" who are qualified under this program shall mean those students of underprivileged families falling below the poverty line as determined by the National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA), who have the ability to continue and finish a degree course. > The beneficiaries under this program shall be entitled to a reasonable monthly stipend depending on costs of licing in a particular educational institution, free tuition, book allowance and other miscellaneous fees to be determined by the administering agency.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION OF PUBLIC BUILDINGS TO ACCOMMODATE THE PHYSICALLY HANDICAPPED
rows.abstract: Rationale: Physical or architectural-b arriers are a primary obstacle in limiting the ability of the disabled to live full meaningful lives. In employment, for instance, anti-discrimina tory statutes enacted for the benefit of the handicapped will be of little practical value when the employer can evade compliance with the law by arguing that the applicant cannot get into the place of employment in the first place. In effect, there is a need to first establish "access" in order to achieve goalof equal employment opportunity.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC WORKS AND HIGHWAYS since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING GOVERNMENT-OWNE D OR -CONTROLLED CORPORATIONS (GOCCs) ON THE PRIVATIZATION PROGRAM TO RESERVE AT LEAST TWENTY PERCENT (20%) OF THEIR TOTAL INITIAL PUBLIC OFFERING (IPO) OF SHARES TO OVERSEAS WORKERS, AUTHORIZING THE OVERSEAS WORKERSINVESTMENT (OWI) FUND UNDER REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7111 TO MANAGE AN INVESTMENT FUND PORTFOLIO FOR OVERSEAS WORKERS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to provide investment opportunities and incentives to the overseas workers and their families by allowing OCWs and their beneficiaries to purchase participatory stocks from an investment fund that will manage their money under a trust arragement.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR GREATER FISCAL AUTONOMY IN FAVOR OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS (LGUs) IN THE CHOICE OF DEPOSITORY BANKS, AMENDING SECTION 311 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.title_short: Providing Local Government Units Autonomy in the Choice of Depository Banks
rows.abstract: Local treasusrers shall maintain depository accounts in the name of their respective local government units with banks DULY ACCREDITED AS SUCH BY THE BANGKO SENTRAL NG PILIPINAS [preferably government-owne d] located in or nearest their respective areas of jurisdiction. Earnings of each depository account shall accrue exlusively thereto.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2002-03-06, transmitted to on 2002-03-11 and received by the Senate on 2002-03-12

second_reading.remarks: The Body approved to consider the Explanatory Note of the original    Bill as the sponsorship remarks on the measure.

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT PRESCRIBING THE PROCEDURE FOR THE EXPEDITIOUS HOLDING OF A SPECIAL ELECTION IN CASE OF VACANCY IN THE CONGRESS OF THE PHILIPPINES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SIXTY-SIX HUNDRED AND FORTY-FIVE, ENTITLED "AN ACT PRRESCRIBINGTHE MANNER OF FILLING OF VACANCY IN THE CONGRESS OF THE PHILIPPINES"
rows.abstract: This bill prescribes the procedure for the expeditious holding of special election, through a certification by the Speaker on the existence of vacancy and calling for a special election to fill the vacancy in a particular legislative district.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE AMOUNT OF SUPPLIES WHICH MAY BE PROCURED BY LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS THROUGH PERSONAL CANVASS, THEREBY AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 367 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160
rows.title_short: Increasing the Amount of Supplies to be Procured by Local Government Units Thru Personal Canvass
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to increase the amount of supplies and equipment items which may be purchased by local government units WITHOUT PUBLIB BIDDING and the approval of the Committee on Awards.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2002-04-23, transmitted to on 2002-04-29 and received by the Senate on 2002-04-30

second_reading.remarks: The Body approved to consider the Explanatory Note of the Bill as the sponsorship remarks.

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT SETTING ASIDE TWENTY-FIVE PERCENT (25%) OF THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS' CALAMITY FUNDS FOR PREPARATORY ACTIVITIES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: With the proposed measure, the amount to be set aside would be used for preparatory activities such as: the dissemination of information on what to do before, during and after the calamity; for the LGUs to pinpoint, reinforce and strengthen relocation centers; for procurement of medicines, blankets, food and other basic necessities; and for other steps to be undertaken to minimize, if not prevent, loss of lives and damage to properties.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT INTRODUCING REFORMS IN THE OPERATIONS OF THE BUREAU OF CUSTOMS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This measure seeks to introduce particular reforms in the Bureau of Customs by modernizing its operations to elevate the same to the level of modern and efficient customs administration of other countries.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO AMEND REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED THREE THOUSAND FOUR HUNDRED FIFTY-SIX, AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED FOUR THOUSAND ONE HUNDRED SEVENTY-SEVEN, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS "INTERNAL AUDITING ACT OF 1962"
rows.abstract: Rationale: The "Internal Auditing Act of 1962" has not been fully implemented. The organization of internal audit services in government offices, agencies and local government units, has also been hampered due to the absence of organizational structures and positions in the government. The government's continuing drive against graft and corruption is perceived as weak because of the non-implementat ion of the Internal Auditing Act. The problem of graft and corruption in the government is well recognized as systemic. It would require the review, audit and the improvement of internal controls in the systems and processes in the government to help address and solve the problem.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2001-07-24

first_reading.comm_act: chnge of cttee. ref'l from Civil Service & Prof'l Regulation

rows.author: D071
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09231) enacted on 2003-12-19
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING AND PENALIZING THE EMPLOYMENT OF CHILDREN IN ANY PUBLIC OR PRIVATE UNDERTAKING OR OCCUPATION WHICH IS CONSIDERED HAZARDOUS TO THEIR LIFE, SAFETY, HEALTH AND MORALS, OR WHICH UNDULY INTERFERES WITH THEIR NORMAL DEVELOPMENT AND FOROTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: It is a well-known fact that, in the Philippines and even in other advanced countries, a signifcant number of chidlren are indiscriminatel y made to participate in economic activities at very young ages. Unscrupulous employers take advantage of their predicament -- luring them to work in industries which are clearly hazardous even by adult standards, where they are practically forced to be engaged in every imaginable work and labor under questionable working conditions. While a few of these children have learned to disengage themselves from the grips of those abusers, the greater number have succumbed to the ill effects of such premature, hazardous and misguided employment.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04235

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT FURTHER AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8291, AMENDING PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1146, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE 'REVISED GOVERNMENT SERVICE INSURANCE ACT OF 1977,' AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: The amendments proposed in this bill are intended to benefit civil service employees who retire, resign or are separated from the service after many years of faithful service.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SIXTY-FIVE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-NINE, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "ANTI-CARNAPPIN G ACT OF 1972"
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to amend Republic Act No. 6539 (the Anti-Carnapping Act of 1972) by requiring owners of motor vehicles and other vehicle parts to show only the proof of ownership in securing clearance for the purpose of transporting these from one island to another.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE RELEASE OF RETIREMENT, SEPARATION PAY AND BENEFITS WITH INTEREST FOR RETIRING OR RESIGNING GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS AND EMPLOYEES WITH ADMINISTRATIVE, CRIMINAL AND CIVIL CASES WHO ARE EVENTUALLY EXONERATED OR CLEARED THEREFROM
rows.abstract: Retiring or resigning government officials and employees with administrative, criminal or civil cases who shall be eventually exonerated or cleared therefrom shall receive their retirment or separation pay and benefits with ADDED COMPOUNDED INTERESTfor the period of their retirement or separation date to the date of the promulgation of the decision on his case.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2003-08-04, transmitted to on 2003-08-05 and received by the Senate on 2003-08-07
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A MORE EXPEDITIOUS ACTION ON LETTERS AND REQUESTS FROM THE PUBLIC, AMENDING SECTION FIVE, PARAGRAPH (a) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6713 AND ADDING THERETO SUBPARAGRAPHS (1),(2),(3) AND (4)
rows.abstract: Rationale: Red tape has always been synonymous with the government bureaucracy. This bill seeks to amend RA No. 6713 (Code of Comduct for Government Employees) in order to AVOID or MINIMIZE RED TAPE in all government offices.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06041

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT ALLOWING THE IMPORTATION OF LIVE ANIMALS, MEAT AND MEAT PRODUCTS ONLY FROM ZONES DECLARED BY THE OFFICE INTERNATIONAL DES EPIZOOTIES (OIE) AS "FMD (FOOT AND MOUTH DISEASE) FREE ZONES WHERE VACCINATION IS NOT PRACTICED"
rows.title_short: The Foot and Mouth Disease Eradication Act of 2003
rows.abstract: Recognizing that the livestock industry has the potential for engendering the development of the countryside and enhancing food security, and serving as an instrument for employment generation and economic growth, it is hereby declared the policy ofthe State to promote the ERADICATION of foot and mouth disease through the prevention of the entry of additional FMD serotypes into the country.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2003-05-21, transmitted to on 2003-05-22 and received by the Senate on 2003-05-27

second_reading.remarks: The Body approved to consider the Explanatory Note of the Bill as the sponsorship remarks.

rows.author: D071
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09174) enacted on 2002-11-07
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED 6768, ENTITLED "AN ACT INSTITUTING A BALIKBAYAN PROGRAM"
rows.abstract: Rationale: Complaints aired by the balikbayans themselves have underscored the need to amend some provisions of the law.  The forty-eight (48) hour limit given the balikbayan under Republic Act No. 6768 to complete his shopping is not sufficient, especially considering such factors as jet lag, tight family schedules and other matters that the balikbayan has to attend to first upon return.  The need to reassess the time limit for shopping is imperative in order to allow the balikbayan ample choice of a convenient shopping time. This proposes amendments to RA 6768 (Balikbayan Law) such as on:  (1) Benefits and privileges of the balikbayan; and on (2) Limitations on purchases.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04534

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THAT ALL LIQUOR PRODUCTS CARRY A WARNING LABEL THAT ALCOHOL INTAKE DURING PREGNANCY IS HAZARDOUS TO THE LIFE AND HEALTH OF THE UNBORN CHILD
rows.abstract: The cost of the additional warning label, such as could be found in cigarette products is relatively small compared to the danger faced by many Filipino children. Approval of this bill could mean the start of a national campaign to foster this needed consciousness among out Filipino mothers.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROMULGATING THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL STANDARDS FOR DRINKING WATER, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: To ensure safety, this bill mandates that water supplied to the public must meet the requirements established by the Philippine National Standards for Drinking Water.  The Secretary of Health shall have the primary authority to enforce the PNSDW.  The bill aims to compel water suppliers to comply with the national standards by providing a reasonable period for compliance and by meeting out penalties of P3,000-P10,000 for the first offense, and P10,000-P20,000 or revocation of license for subsequent offenses.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE NATIONAL INSTITUTE FOR SCIENCE AND MATHEMATICS EDUCATION DEVELOPMENT (NISMED), APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This proposed bill will create the National Institute for Science and Mathematics Educational Development (NISMED) to specifically upgrade research by investigating the conditions under which science and mathematics are best learned and taught, develop appropriate teaching and learning materials and professionalize teachers, educators, supervisors and school administrators.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING A MECHANISM FOR GENERATING QUALITY GRADUATES OF HIGHER EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS BASED ON PERFORMANCE IN PROFESSIONAL LICENSURE EXAMINATIONS
rows.abstract: "Professional Examination Zero - Performance Policy Act." Rationale: The State shall provide for appropriate safeguards to maintain the high quality of professional education by arresting the perceived decline in the quality of higher education brought about by the continued onslaught of commercializati on of education in higher education institutions whose administrations are more inclined to maximize the tuition revenues than the provision of a sound and competent higher education.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT INTITUTIONALIZI NG THE OPENING OF NIGHT CLASSES USING EXISTING HIGH SCHOOL AND ELEMENTARY SCHOOL FACILITIES ALL OVER THE COUNTRY AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to institutionaliz e the opening of Night High School classes using existing high school and elementary school facilities throughout the country.  The purpose of this bill is to address the recurreing problem of lack of school buildings and other facilities and teachers for public secondary education. Because of the lack of secondary schools, the number of out-of-school youth and dropouts has increased.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ENTITLE CHILDREN OF TEACHERS AND EMPLOYEES IN PUBLIC AND PRIVATE INSTITUTIONS OF HIGHER LEARNING TO FREE TUITION AND OTHER SCHOOL FEES
rows.abstract: Rationale:  If government and private institutions of higher learning, because of their own financial limitations, cannot give their teachers decent pay to help them send their children to college, other remedies have to resorted to. This bill seeksto provide one such remedy: exempt children of teachers in public and private secondary institutions of higher learning from paying tuition and other school fees when they enroll at the educational institutions where one or both of their parents areteaching.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT IMPOSING A TEN PERCENT (10%) COMPUTER EDUCATION TAX ON RECEIPTS (EXCLUDING VALUE-ADDED TAX) FROM CELLULAR PHONE CALLS TO BE BORNE BY CELLULAR PHONE COMPANIES, CREATING A SPECIAL COMPUTER LITERACY EDUCATION FUND FOR PUBLIC SCHOOLS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill proposes to impose a fifty-centavo tax on everu call charged by a cellular company to its subscribers to start-up and finance the computer literacy education program in public schools nationwide. Our public schools should very well producequality and computer-litera te graduates. It is the call of the times, our youth need not lag behind their counterparts in the private schools and other countries so as to maintain the high literacy level our people should have in this era of Information Technology.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2003-08-04, transmitted to on 2003-08-05 and received by the Senate on 2003-08-07
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZ ING THE NON-FORMAL EDUCATION ACCREDITATION AND EQUIVALENCY (NFE A&E) SYSTEM, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREOF AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The role of non-formal education (NFE) in the development of the literacy and vocational skills of drop-outs and out-of-school youth has been acknowledged as one of the major avenues to uplift the socio-economic condition of the masses. The non-formal education learning center will serve as the specific venue for conducting non-formal education sich as basic literacy education, vocational skills training, values development and other socio-cultural activities. The NFE learning center will alsoserve as the community library.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06033

rows.author: D071
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2003-02-10, transmitted to on 2002-02-10 and received by the Senate on 2003-02-13
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS WHICH OFFER COURSES REQUIRING PROFESSIONAL EXAMINATIONS FROM COMPELLING THEIR GRADUATES TO TAKE REVIEW CLASSES AND/OR PRE-LICENSURE EXAMINATIONS IN THE EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTION OF WHICH HE IS A GRADUATE ANDPROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: Many student-graduat es decry certain objectionable practices by educational institutions offering courses requiring board, bar or any licensing examination. One of these practices is to compel the graduate to take review classes in the same educational institution of which he or she is a graduate under pain of delaying the release of transcripts or scholastic records. Considering the Constitutional provisions on the protection and promotion of education, it would be better to enhance and strengthen the same by granting these graduates the right to freely choose the educational institutions wherein they would take their review classes.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05326

rows.author: D017
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE CONSTRUCTION OF A SOLDIERS' MEMORIAL MONUMENT IN THE RIZAL PARK, AUTHORIZING THE APPROPRIATION OF FUNDS THEREFOR ANF FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC WORKS AND HIGHWAYS since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING OTHER PRIVILEGES AND INCENTIVES TO PERSONS WITH DISABILITY, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE "MAGNA CARTA FOR DISABLED PERSONS"
rows.title_short: Granting other Privileges and Incentives to Persons with Disability
rows.abstract: Persons with disabilities are as vulnerable as the senior citizens. They should be given the same privileges enjoyed by senior citiznes.  Not only would this surely boost their morale but this would make them feel that they are valued members of thesociety and not a burden to their families.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2002-05-23, transmitted to on 2002-05-28 and received by the Senate on 2002-05-28

second_reading.remarks: The Body approved to consider the Explanatory Note of the Bill as the sponsorship remarks.

rows.author: D017
rows.mother_status: Business for the day on 2004-02-04
rows.title_full: AN ACT IMPLEMENTING THE RIGHT OF ACCESS TO INFORMATION ON MATTERS OF PUBLIC CONCERN GUARANTEED UNDER SECTION SEVEN, ARTICLE III OF THE 1987 CONSTITUTION AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The following shall be made available for public scrutiny: records, documents, papers, research materials, tapes, microfilm, videotapes and the like, statements of policy and interpretations thereof, final opinions, as well as orders made in the adjudication of cases, administrative staff manuals and instructions affecting the public which are kept in or under the executive branch of the government, including the Office of the President, government research institutions, local governments, themilitary establishment and government-owne d or controlled corporations which are hereinafter referred to as government agencies.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06671

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT PENALIZING THE NEGATIVE PORTRAYAL OF A PERSON WITH A DISABILITY IN MOVIES, TELEVISION, STAGE AND OTHER FORMS OF MASS COMMUNICATION
rows.abstract: "Media Protection for the Disabled Act."  Any person who, in the performance of an act before the television, movies, stage, and other similar forms of mass communication, shall intentionally or maliciously mock, embarrass, humiliate, or otherwise insult a person with disabilities shall be penalized with imprisonment of not more than six (6) months and/or, a fine not exceeding Five thousand pesos (P5,000.00)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC INFORMATION since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09167) enacted on 2002-06-07
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE FILM DEVELOPMENT AND INCENTIVES BOARD, DEFINING ITS POWERS  AND FUNCTIONS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This piece of legislation seeks to foster the development, promotion and growth of the local film industry by providing tax incentives to good quality films.  Its goal is to improve the artistic and technical quality of the local film industry.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04644

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE ARTISTS CAREER SERVICE, RECOGNIZING THE SPECIAL QUALIFICATIONS OF ARTISTS IN GOVERNMENT, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The Artists Career Service is a system of recruitment, career progression, recognition and reward of artists in the public service, and a means of selecting, developing and retaining a pool of highly qualified and productive artists personnel. Members of the Service, from the first, second and third levels, shall be granted eligibilities corresponding to the regular career service.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2002-09-03, transmitted to on 2002-09-03 and received by the Senate on 2002-09-03
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ESTABLISH AND MAINTAIN AN OFFICE OF VETERANS AFFAIRS IN THE PHILIPPINE EMBASSY IN THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA, PRESCRIBING ITS FUNCTIONS, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to formally institutionaliz e the Office of Veterans Affairs in the Philippine Embassy in the United States, to fix its term of existence and appropriate funds for its administration and operation.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04844

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXTENDING PREFERENCE OF EMPLOYMENT TO ANY ONE CHILD OF VETERANS IN THE GOVERNMENT, INCLUDING GOVERNMENT-OWNE D OR -CONTROLLED CORPORATIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Extending Preference of Employment to Any One Child of Veterans in the Government
rows.abstract: All government agencies, including government-owne d and/or-controll ed corporations, shall hire or employ any child of a veteran: Provided, That in the absence or disqualificatio n of said child, a grandchild shall be hired or employed in his stead.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2002-09-03, transmitted to on 2002-09-03 and received by the Senate on 2002-09-03

second_reading.remarks: The Body approved to consider the Explanatory Note of the Bill  as    the sponsorship remarks.

rows.author: D071
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2002-05-07, transmitted to on 2002-05-09 and received by the Senate on 2002-05-13
rows.title_full: AN ACT REDEFINING THE TERM "VETERAN" THEREBY AMENDING FURTHER REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6948, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to clarify the definition of "VETERAN" in order to reconcile inconsistencies in the definition as stated in RAs 6948, 7696 vis-a-vis Section 7 of the Constitution.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04457

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PAYMENT THROUGH VETERANS BONDS OF ARREARAGES IN THE VETERANS PENSIONS AS MANDATED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7696 AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The Secretary of Finance, with the approval of the President of the Philippines, after consultation with the Monetary Board, is authorized to issue Veterans Bonds, in accordance with Section 1 of Republic Act No. 245, as amended, and Section 123 ofR. A> No. 7653, to meet the payment of the arrearages in the veterans pensions as mandated by R.A. No. 7696 amounting to Ten billion nine hundred twenty nine million nine hundred forty three thousand seven hundred ninety five pesos (P10,929,943,79 5.00)

rows.author: D071
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2002-05-07, transmitted to on 2002-05-09 and received by the Senate on 2002-05-13
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE BOOKS FOR THE BARRIOS PROGRAM AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: It is hereby declared the policy of the State to give the Filipino youth, particularly in remote areas, the chance for upward mobility through education not only by listening but also by reading. Towards this end, all public schools and libraries inremote barangays shall be provided with books under the Books for the Barrios Program.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04561

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING LOCAL SCHOOL BOARDS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTIONS 98, 99 AND 100 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale:  It is a well known fact that the Minority in any Sanggunian represents the other side in the community. They are fiscalizers in the disbursement of funds and the promulgation of laws in the Sanggunian and their presence in the Local School Board will give added assurance that the administration of this special fund is subjected to the scrutiny and safeguard that it deserves. Also, this will help promote the general support to programs formulated by the Board and will contribute to asound local governance.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT DESIGNATING THE TECHNOLOGY MANAGEMENT CENTER OF THE UNIVERSITY OF THE PHILIPPINES AT DILIMAN, QUEZON CITY, AS A NATIONAL CENTER OF EXCELLENCE FOR TECHNOLOGY ASSESSMENT, MANAGEMENT, FORECASTING , AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO INTEGRATE INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY EDUCATION INTO THE PUBLIC ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY CURRICULA AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: In the Philippines, computers are already prevalent in the working place.  If our youth are to be fully equipped to face the business world confidently and with a bright outlook to the future, they must, at the very least, be computer-litera te.  Graduates who are computer illiterate often find themselves at a disadvantage when faced with their computer-litera te counterparts. Being knowledgeable on computers can make them competitive and responsive in the job market.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING TO USE THE ENGLISH LANGUAGE AS THE MEDIUM OF COMMUNICATION IN ALL GOVERNMENT-SPON SORED EXAMINATIONS
rows.abstract: The English language shall be used as the medium of communication in all government-spon sored examinations with the exception of the licensure examination for professional teachers, the scope of which include Pilipino subject.

rows.author: D071
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09255) enacted on 2004-02-24
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLE 176 OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 209, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE FAMILY CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES (RE: FATHER'S SURNAME)
rows.abstract: ILLEGITIMATE CHILDREN MAY USE THE SURNAME OF THEIR FATHER IF THEIR FILIATION HAS BEEN EXPRESSLY RECOGNIZED BY THE FATHER THROUGH THE RECORD OF BIRTH APPEARING IN THE CIVIL REGISTER; OR AN ADMISSION IN A PUBLIC DOCUMENT OR A PRIVATE HANDWRITTEN INSTRUMENT AND SIGNED BY THE PUTATIVE FATHER, UNLESS DEOXYRIBONUCLEI C ACID (DNA) TEST RESULTS DISPROVES SUCH FILIATION.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04437

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLES 96, 124, 211 AND 225 OF THE NEW FAMILY CODE TO PROVIDE FOR JUDICIAL INTERVENTION IN CASES OF DISAGREEMENT BETWEEN HUSBAND AND WIFE OVER THE ADMINISTRATION AND ENJOYMENT OF COMMUNITY PROPERTY, THE ADMINISTRATION AND ENJOYMENTOF CONJUGAL PARTNERSHIP PROPERTY AND THE EXERCISE OF PARENTAL AUTHORITY AND LEGAL GUARDIANSHIP OVER THE PERSON AND PROPERTY OF UNEMANCIPATED COMMON CHILD
rows.abstract: Rationale: The Family Code " largely adopted gender-fair provisions," but still "retained provisions giving due advantage to the husband over the wife."  This proposed measure, therefore, seeks to correct this inequity.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2002-05-23, transmitted to on 2002-05-28 and received by the Senate on 2002-05-28
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE LEGITIMATION OF CHILDREN BORN TO PARENTS BELOW MARRYING AGE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE FAMILY CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: This bill proposes to amend Article 177 of EO No. 209, as follows: "Art. 177. Only children conceived and born outside of wedlock of parents who, at the time of the conception of the former, were not disqualified by any impediment to marry each other, EXCEPT BY IMPEDIMENT OF BEING UNDERAGE, may be legitimated."
rows.status: Substituted by HB04538

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLE 34 OF THE FAMILY CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES OR EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 209
rows.abstract: Article 34 of the Family Code of the Philippines or Executive Order No. 209, is hereby amended to read as follows: "Article 34. No license shall be necessary for the marriage of a man and woman who have lived together as husband and wife for at least 5 years and without any legal impediment to marry each other.  The contracting parties shall state the foregoing facts in an affidavit before any person authorized by law to administer oaths: PROVIDED, THAT IN CASE EITHER OR BOTH OF THE CONTRACTINGPARTIES ARE BETWEEN THE AGES OF EIGHTEEN AND TWENTY-ONE, OR BETWEEN THE AGES OF TWENTY-ONE AND TWENTY-FIVE, THEY SHALL FURTHER STATE IN THE AFFIDAVIT THAT THEY COMPLIED WITH THE REQUIREMENTS ON PARENTAL CONSENT OR PARENTAL ADVICE PROVIDED FOR UNDERARTICLE 14 OR 15, AS THE CASE MAY BE. The solemnizing officer shall also state under oath that he ascertained the qualifications of the contracting parties and found no legal impediment to the marriage.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D071
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2002-04-23, transmitted to on 2002-04-29 and received by the Senate on 2002-04-30
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 122-A, AS AMENDED BY EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 295, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE ACT CREATING THE OFFICE ON MUSLIM AFFAIRS
rows.abstract: Rationale:  In the past years, the conduct of Hajj was marred with irregularities and charges of mismanagement as aired in various complaints from Muslim pilgrims.  The perennial problems encountered ranged from the failure of intending pilgrims tojoin the Hajj citing administrative lapses by responsible government agency, the amount of fees required, delays in the processing and issuance of travel documents, to airline and billeting accomodations, among others. This bill seeks to address these problems.
rows.status: Substituted by HB00078

rows.author: D071
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09177) enacted on 2002-11-13
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING THE FIRST DAY OF SHAWAL, THE TENTH MONTH OF THE MUSLIM CALENDAR, A NATIONAL HOLIDAY FOR THE OBSERVANCE OF EIDUL-FITR, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 26, CHAPTER 7 OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 292, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE ADMINISTRATIVE CODE OF 1987, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The first day of Shawal, the tenth month of the Muslim calendar, is hereby declared as a national holiday for the observance of EIDUL-FITR. This is the first day marking the end of the thirty-day fasting period of Ramadhan.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04373

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE USE OF THE WORDS `MUSLIM' AND `CHRISTIAN' IN PRINT AND BROADCAST MEDIA TO DESCRIBE ANY PERSON SUSPECTED OF OR CONVICTED FOR HAVING COMMITTED CRIMINAL OR UNLAWFUL ACT AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to prohibit the use of the words "Muslim" and "Christian" in print and broadcast media to described any person suspected of or convicted of having committed criminal or unlawful acts, and provides for penalties for violation thereof.The words "Muslim" and "Christian" refer to a person's religious belief and do not in any way refer to a person's place of origin or propensity for criminal behavior.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2002-05-23, transmitted to on 2002-05-28 and received by the Senate on 2002-05-28
